tasks.short: Choose books, crafts and songs, prepare materials, read, paint, draw and sing with the children, and share photos with parents.

steps.what: Childcare worker chooses books, crafts and songs for the week from children's interests

loop.input: An interest the worker has logged for the group (for example, tractors or rain), the age band and the centre's pedagogical goals list.
loop.output: Three activity ideas: a book theme, a craft with materials list, and a song or rhyme.
loop.check: Each idea must name a goal from the centre's pedagogical plan; materials must be on the centre's supply list; no child names or personal data go in; the worker edits before use.
loop.stop: One draft and one redraft; then the worker chooses from the library.
loop.why_not_simpler: Turning a child's interest into fresh activities is creative work; a library only offers what is already there.

steps.what: Childcare worker prepares paint, paper and craft materials
Childcare worker reads to children
Childcare worker guides simple painting, drawing and handicrafts
Childcare worker teaches songs to the group
Childcare worker posts activity photos in the parents' chat group

tasks.design: A bounded step drafts activity ideas from an interest the worker logged and the centre's pedagogical goals, and the worker edits them. Photos go into the parent app's diary in the childcare management system ({OTHER}), which only shows them to parents who consented, instead of a chat group; reading, crafts and songs stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Ideas came from memory and photos went into chat groups without consent checks.
tasks.enabler_now: Early-years tools draft activity ideas from a child's interest, and Dutch parent apps hold a diary with photo consent.
tasks.still_hard: Drafts must suit the age and the room; consent must be set per child.
tasks.human_edge: Reading a story so a toddler is spellbound and letting a child's own idea lead the craft.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes; preparation is quicker and photo sharing safer.

reach.task: Plan activities for a family's children
reach.learn: Whether interest-based drafts work outside a centre.

evidence.claim: An early-years tool drafts activity ideas from an area of learning or a child's interest; educators check them.
A Dutch parent app shows a timeline, daily report and photos and asks parents for photo and diary consent at first login.
Parent-facing chatbots must disclose AI; drafting activity ideas is not a listed high-risk use.

assumptions: Boundary: from choosing activities to sharing photos; observations of development are outside.

Input contract: pedagogical goals list and supply list kept by the centre manager; interests logged by workers without child names; photo consent recorded by parents in the app; fallback is the activity binder and paper.
Reading, crafts and songs do not change.
No child data goes into the drafting step.
unknowns: Whether the centre uses a parent app.
research_questions: Do interest-based activities hold children's attention longer?

already_counted.description: Childcare worker edits drafted activity ideas.

incremental.description: Childcare worker logs group interests for the draft.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Workers with a good activity library and no photo sharing save little.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep rules and tidy-up routines, redirect children, talk with colleagues, note behaviour for parents and discuss it at pick-up.

steps.what: Childcare worker repeats group rules and tidy-up routines such as picking up toys and books
Childcare worker redirects and disciplines children in the moment
Childcare worker discusses repeated behavior with colleagues at handover
Childcare worker writes behaviour notes in the child's paper notebook
Childcare worker talks with parents about behaviour at pick-up

tasks.design: The paper notebook becomes a short daily diary entry in the parent app of the childcare management system ({OTHER}), visible to colleagues on the next shift. Rules, redirection and conversations stay in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes lived in a paper notebook that went home with the child.
tasks.enabler_now: Dutch parent apps hold a daily diary shared with parents and staff.
tasks.still_hard: Guiding behaviour is relationship work; written notes about behaviour need care and tact.
tasks.human_edge: Staying calm with an angry toddler and helping them find words.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes; notes are quicker and shared.

reach.task: Follow up children with repeated behaviour problems
reach.learn: Whether shared diary notes surface patterns earlier.

evidence.claim: A Dutch parent app gives parents a daily report in a digital diary.
Apps that time-stamp each staff action can monitor performance and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from daily routines to the parent talk; formal concerns procedures are outside.
Input contract: diary set up by the centre manager with parent consent; fallback is the paper notebook.
Diary entries are not used to judge staff.
Rules, redirection and talks do not change.
unknowns: How often behaviour notes are written.
research_questions: Do shared notes make staff responses more consistent?

incremental.description: Childcare worker learns the diary entry screen.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Almost all of this task is in-person guidance; only notes change.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan outings and games, get approval, collect parent consent, book transport, check ratio and allergies, and lead the activity.

steps.what: Childcare worker plans outings and games with colleagues
Centre manager approves the outing
Childcare worker collects paper permission slips for field trips from parents
Childcare worker books transport or tickets by phone
Childcare worker checks the staff-child ratio and allergy list for the outing on paper
Childcare worker leads the recreational games and outings

tasks.design: Permission requests go out through the parent app of the childcare management system ({OTHER}), which lists who has replied, and the same system shows the staff-child ratio for the children registered for the day and their allergy notes. Planning, booking and leading the outing stay with the worker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Permission slips and allergy lists were paper and checked by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Childcare systems hold attendance, allergy notes and parent messages.
tasks.still_hard: Outings carry safety risk; allergy notes are health data that only the right staff may see.
tasks.human_edge: Keeping a group of small children safe and happy in a busy place.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; checks are quicker.

evidence.claim: A Dutch parent app shows parents a timeline, daily report and agenda and handles consent.
Allergy notes are special-category data and need a processor contract for any tool that holds them.

assumptions: Boundary: from planning to leading the outing; incident handling is outside.
Input contract: registrations per day and allergy notes kept by the centre administration; ratio rules set by the centre manager; fallback is paper slips and lists.
Centre manager time is outside the worker's savings.
Planning, booking and leading do not change.
research_questions: Do app permissions arrive faster than paper slips?

already_counted.description: Childcare worker checks the list of permission replies.

incremental.description: Childcare worker sets up the permission request in the app.

approvals.approved_version: The outing, date and cost as approved by the centre manager in s2; changes need a new approval before booking.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Centres with few outings, or parents who do not use the app, save little.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Set up a homework corner, find out what each child has to do, help with school work, and tell parents what was done.

steps.what: Childcare worker sets up a quiet homework corner
Childcare worker asks each child what homework they have
Childcare worker helps children with homework and school work
Childcare worker looks up how the school explains a method
Childcare worker tells parents at pick-up what homework was done

tasks.design: Parents note the day's homework in the parent app of the childcare management system ({OTHER}), the worker ticks what was done, and parents see it there. A short sheet from the local schools on how they teach common methods sits in {DOCS}; helping children stays in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Homework was known only from what children remembered, and updates were told at the door.
tasks.enabler_now: Parent apps hold short notes both ways.
tasks.still_hard: Each school teaches methods differently, and children need patient help.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a tired child finish their sums without doing it for them.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes; less guessing and repeating at the door.

reach.learn: Whether parent notes help tutors prepare.

evidence.claim: A Dutch parent app offers a digital diary and agenda shared with parents.
AI that evaluates children's learning would be high-risk; this design uses none.

assumptions: Boundary: from setting up to telling parents; tutoring by schools is outside.
Input contract: homework notes entered by parents; method sheets provided by the local schools and kept by the centre manager; fallback is asking the children.
Parent time is outside the worker's savings.
unknowns: Share of parents who would note homework.
Number of children doing homework at the centre.
research_questions: Do children finish more homework when it is listed in advance?

incremental.description: Childcare worker ticks homework done in the app.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Groups where children know their homework well save almost nothing.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The childcare worker keeps play, care, guidance and homework help; notebooks, slips and chat groups move into the parent app.
role.ambitious_version: A childcare worker whose paperwork fits in the parent app and whose day is spent with the children.
